title: NCLAT Upholds Mastana Foods Resolution Plan, Dismisses Rival Bidder's and Promoters' Appeals
meta_description: NCLAT dismisses five appeals against the NCLT's approval of Mastana Foods' resolution plan, holding the CoC's commercial wisdom is not open to appeal.
court: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi
bench: Justice Mohd Faiz Alam Khan (Judicial Member) and Naresh Salecha (Technical Member)
case_name: Amba Grains Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. v. Amit Agrawal, Resolution Professional of Mastana Foods Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
body: Mastana Foods Private Limited, a Delhi-based food business, was admitted into the corporate insolvency resolution process back in 2019, on a petition brought by the State Bank of India. The case moved slowly even by the standards of insolvency litigation in India, and it was only in June 2026 that the NCLT's Delhi bench approved a resolution plan for the company, worth roughly Rs. 135.39 crore, submitted jointly by HR Commercials Private Limited and Crown Steels. That approval should ordinarily have closed the matter and let the new promoters take over the company, but it instead triggered a fresh round of litigation before the appellate tribunal.

Five appeals were filed against the NCLT's order. Amba Grains Private Limited, which had itself submitted a resolution plan for Mastana Foods and lost out to the HR Commercials-Crown Steels consortium, challenged the approval as an unsuccessful bidder with an obvious commercial stake in the outcome. Separately, Anil Khurana and Krishan Mohan Mendiratta, suspended directors of the corporate debtor who also stood as personal guarantors for its debts, filed their own appeals. Both sets of appellants asked the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal to set aside the NCLT's approval of the resolution plan and send the process back for reconsideration, each pressing a different version of the same complaint.

A bench of Justice Mohd Faiz Alam Khan and Naresh Salecha heard all five appeals together, under case numbers running from 1114 to 1198 of 2026, and dismissed each of them, finding no ground to interfere with the NCLT's approval. The tribunal did not find any infirmity in the way the Committee of Creditors had evaluated the competing plans, or in the process by which it settled on the HR Commercials-Crown Steels plan over Amba Grains' own bid. On that finding, the Rs. 135.39 crore plan approved in June 2026 stands, and the appellants' attempt to reopen the process failed at the appellate stage as well.

The reasoning tracks a line the Supreme Court has held to consistently in cases on the commercial wisdom of a Committee of Creditors: once that committee has voted to approve a resolution plan, neither the adjudicating authority nor the appellate tribunal sits as a court of appeal over that commercial judgment. The NCLT's role under Section 30(2) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code is to check that the plan meets the statute's own requirements, not to second-guess which of the competing plans was commercially superior. The NCLAT's role on appeal, under Section 32 read with Section 61(3), is correspondingly narrow. Unless an appellant can point to one of the specific statutory grounds for interference, a plan that has cleared the CoC's vote and the NCLT's compliance check is not something the tribunal will reopen on its own assessment of the merits.

That reasoning cuts particularly hard against Amba Grains' position. Having lost out to a rival bidder in the resolution process, it had no independent legal ground to fall back on beyond arguing that its own plan, or the process generally, deserved a second look, and that is exactly the kind of argument the tribunal has repeatedly said is not open to an unsuccessful resolution applicant. The suspended directors fared no better before the bench. Being a personal guarantor for the corporate debtor's loans gives a stake in the outcome, but it does not translate into a right to relitigate the CoC's commercial assessment of which plan to accept, and the tribunal treated their appeals on that footing.

With the appeals dismissed, the resolution plan approved for Mastana Foods in June 2026 is now final at the appellate stage, clearing the way for HR Commercials and Crown Steels to implement it and take over the company. For resolution applicants who lose out in a competitive process, and for suspended promoters hoping an appeal might reopen a plan they would rather avoid, the order is one more instance of the appellate tribunal declining to treat an adverse commercial outcome, by itself, as a legal wrong that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code lets it correct.
why_it_matters: The ruling reinforces that an unsuccessful resolution applicant's dissatisfaction with losing a competitive bidding process, or a suspended director's interest as a personal guarantor, is not a ground on its own to reopen a resolution plan once the Committee of Creditors has approved it and the NCLT has checked it for statutory compliance. For lenders and resolution applicants, it confirms that a plan cleared by the CoC's commercial vote carries real finality at the appellate stage, narrowing the window for a disappointed bidder or promoter to delay implementation through a fresh round of litigation.
card_summary: NCLAT dismisses five appeals by a rival bidder and the suspended directors of Mastana Foods against the NCLT's approval of its Rs. 135.39 crore resolution plan, citing the CoC's commercial wisdom.
card_tip: Losing a resolution bid, or standing as a personal guarantor, is not by itself a ground to appeal a CoC-approved plan; appellate review is confined to statutory compliance, not commercial merits.
verification_notes: The underlying facts, the NCLAT bench (Justice Mohd Faiz Alam Khan and Naresh Salecha), the appellants (Amba Grains Private Limited, and suspended directors Anil Khurana and Krishan Mohan Mendiratta), the dismissal of all five appeals, and the tribunal's reasoning on the limited scope of appellate review over a CoC-approved plan are confirmed by two independent reports, from PSU Watch and Legal Suvidha, describing the same ruling. The appeal numbers and party names (Amba Grains Pvt. Ltd. v. Amit Agrawal, Resolution Professional of Mastana Foods Pvt. Ltd.) are confirmed against an NCLAT cause list. The NCLT Delhi's approval of the Rs. 135.39 crore resolution plan from HR Commercials Private Limited and Crown Steels in June 2026 is confirmed by a LiveLawBiz report on that NCLT order. The decision date of 15 October 2026 rests on the publication date of both news reports rather than a copy of the NCLAT order itself, which could not be independently retrieved; this is flagged as the weakest-confirmed fact in the piece, though it is consistent with the matter being shown as reserved 'for judgment' on an NCLAT cause list from August 2026. No monetary figure beyond the Rs. 135.39 crore plan value, stated by both sources, is used.
